title: What do flatMapToInt, flatMapToLong, and flatMapToDouble do: map each element to a primitive stream and flatten: and when are they preferred over flatMap(...).mapToInt(...)?
shortTitle: flatMapToInt/Long/Double: flatten to primitive stream, vs flatMap+mapToInt
keyPoints: flatMapToInt maps each element to an IntStream and flattens all resulting IntStreams into one
It is the primitive equivalent of flatMap, avoiding the intermediate Stream<Integer> boxing
Preferred when each element produces multiple primitive values that will be aggregated
flatMap+mapToInt creates an intermediate object stream with boxing; flatMapToInt avoids this
flatMapToLong and flatMapToDouble work identically for long and double primitives
Use flatMapToInt when flattening to numbers and then aggregating for both clarity and performance

s1_definition.oneliner: flatMapToInt maps each element to an IntStream and flattens all resulting primitive streams into one, avoiding the boxing that flatMap+mapToInt would create.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **flatMapToInt(Function<T, IntStream>)** – maps each element to an IntStream and concatenates all resulting IntStreams into one IntStream.
- **Zero boxing** – elements go directly from source to primitive stream without Integer wrapper objects.
- **vs flatMap+mapToInt** – flatMap returns Stream<Integer> (boxing), then mapToInt unboxes. flatMapToInt skips the intermediate boxing.
- **Analogues** – flatMapToLong and flatMapToDouble work the same for long and double primitives.
s1_definition.analogy: Each bank account has multiple daily transaction amounts. flatMapToInt opens each account's transaction list and puts all amounts on one primitive conveyor belt with no gift-wrapping (boxing). flatMap+mapToInt would first put wrapped amounts on a gift belt, then unwrap them: extra step, extra wrapping.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  flatMapToInt pipeline:

  Stream<Account>:
    Account(SAV2001, [5000, 3000, 7000])
    Account(CUR3001, [15000, 8000])

  flatMapToInt(a -> IntStream.of(a.dailyAmounts())):
    IntStream: 5000, 3000, 7000, 15000, 8000

  .sum() → 38000
  Zero Integer wrapper objects created.
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
flatMapToInt, flatMapToLong, and flatMapToDouble map each element to a primitive stream and flatten in one step, avoiding the intermediate boxing that flatMap+mapToInt would create. The pattern is `collection.stream().flatMapToInt(item -> IntStream.of(item.getPrimitiveArray())).sum()`.

Use flatMapToInt when flattening to numbers and then aggregating. It is both clearer and more efficient than the two-step flatMap+boxed+mapToInt approach, especially for large datasets where boxing creates GC pressure.

Remember one sentence: flatMapToInt flattens each element to a primitive IntStream in one step with zero boxing, unlike flatMap+mapToInt which boxes in between.
